title: Open immersions and open restriction for $f^!$
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. All schemes and morphisms below are in the standing setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: schemes are separated and of finite type over $k$, and morphisms are $k$-morphisms. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ be admissible, with the condensed coefficient convention and localizing closures of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Put $\mathcal T_T=\Loc(\Dctf(T,\Lambda))\subset D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$, where $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $\Dctf$ means bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Write $f^!$ for the compactification-independent Brown right adjoint on these categories [det-sf-existence-brown], and $j_!=D(j_!)$ for levelwise extension by zero [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek; sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek].

1. For a quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\to X$ with $X$ qcqs [def-weil-open-immersion; def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], the functor $j_!:\mathcal T_U\to\mathcal T_X$ is left adjoint to $j^*:\mathcal T_X\to\mathcal T_U$, and $j^!\simeq j^*$ canonically, compatibly with the adjunctions.
2. For $f:X\to Y$ separated of finite type, an open immersion $v:V\to Y$, $X_V=f^{-1}(V)$, $u:X_V\to X$ and $f_V:X_V\to V$, there is a canonical isomorphism $u^*f^!\simeq f_V^!v^*$ of functors $\mathcal T_Y\to\mathcal T_{X_V}$; for an open $j:U\to X$ there is a canonical isomorphism $j^*f^!\simeq(fj)^!$ of functors $\mathcal T_Y\to\mathcal T_U$.
3. A morphism in $\mathcal T_X$ is an isomorphism as soon as its restrictions to the members of an open covering $X=\bigcup_aU_a$ are. The preceding canonical comparisons compute the restrictions of $f^!$ on $X$ and $Y$: $j_a^*f^!\simeq(fj_a)^!$, and for $Y=\bigcup_bV_b$, $u_b^*f^!\simeq f_{V_b}^!v_b^*$.

proof.text: On module sheaves over the same pulled-back ring $\Lambda$, [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] supplies the exact functor $j_!$ and the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], module pullback $j^*$ is exact and canonically naturally isomorphic to the lift of $j^{-1}$ whose $\Lambda_U$-action is transported along $\alpha_j^{-1}:\Lambda_U\to j^{-1}\Lambda_X$. This is an identification of module functors, not a literal equality of their ring actions. For either additive exact functor $H=j_!,j^*$, [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $H^n(HK)\cong H(H^nK)$ naturally, hence $H$ sends every quasi-isomorphism to a quasi-isomorphism. Termwise application therefore gives $D(H)$ on the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Additivity also preserves chain homotopies: applying $H$ to $a-b=dh+hd$ gives $H(a)-H(b)=H(d)H(h)+H(h)H(d)$. Thus the same functor is defined on the homotopy categories used to index the following systems. We check directly the derived-existence hypotheses in [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors]. For its right-derived ind-system at $K$, write an index as $s:K\to K'$. The map $D(H)(s)$ is invertible; set $p_s=D(H)(s)^{-1}:HK'\to HK$, take the identity index $s_0=\mathrm{id}_K$ and the splitting $HK\to HK$ to be the identity. Naturality follows from $ts=s'$. For the condition in [def-pc-essentially-constant-ind-diagram] take the common target index $s$ itself, using the arrows $s_0\to s$ and $\mathrm{id}_s$: the prescribed composite is $D(H)(s)D(H)(s)^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_{HK'}$. Dually, at a left-derived pro-index $s:M'\to M$, put $u_s=D(H)(s)^{-1}:HM\to HM'$, choose the identity index and identity retraction, and take the common source index $s$ itself. The composite in [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram] is $D(H)(s)^{-1}D(H)(s)=\mathrm{id}_{HM'}$. Thus the right and left total derived functors are everywhere defined with value $D(H)$, by the very definitions used in the derived-adjunction theorem. Apply [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] with $G=j_!$, $F=j^*$: it gives $D(j_!)\dashv D(j^*)$ on the unbounded module-object derived categories. Its canonical adjunction is induced by the specified sheaf adjunction. Write $j^*=D(j^*)$ for this termwise module restriction. No resolution-existence assertion from the changed exact-functor clause is used.

source.place: Tag 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors; blueprint item proof (1), first sentence. Derived existence verified directly by the identity quasi-isomorphism in the defining systems (Categories Tag 05PU), using exact cohomology (Tag 010N).

proof.text: By [det-proper-image-localizing-open], $D(j_!)$ preserves $\Dctf$, sums and the localizing hulls; [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback] gives the same hull preservation for $j^*$. Both restricted functors therefore exist. The subcategories $\mathcal T_U,\mathcal T_X$ are full by [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For $M\in\mathcal T_U$, $N\in\mathcal T_X$, their Hom sets are the ambient Hom sets, so the step 1 bijection $\Hom(j_!M,N)\cong\Hom(M,j^*N)$ restricts, with the same naturality and triangle identities. This proves the adjunction on precisely the localizing categories in clause (1).

source.place: Proof (1), preservation of the localizing subcategories and restriction of the adjunction.

proof.text: The compact-generation hypotheses for the Brown adjunction are supplied by [sk-lem-brown-hypotheses] for every standing source scheme. Compute the lower shriek for $j$ using $U\xrightarrow jX\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}_X}X$, which is a compactification in the sense of [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]: $j$ is quasi-compact open and the identity is proper. By [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek] its functor is $R(\mathrm{id}_X)_*D(j_!)=D(j_!)$; the equality uses the termwise identity functor. The identity-index argument for an exact functor in step 1, applied to the identity pushforward, identifies its total right derived functor canonically with the identity, so no additional resolution hypothesis is needed here. Step 2 exhibits $j^*$ as a right adjoint of this functor. Clause (3) of [det-sf-existence-brown] now gives the unique adjunction-compatible isomorphism $j^!\simeq j^*$, including transport from the chosen compactification. Thus the comparison is canonical with respect to both unit and counit, not an arbitrary isomorphism of functors.

source.place: Proof (1), trivial compactification and uniqueness; compactification is as in sk-def-nagata-sketch-data.

proof.text:
The compact-generation hypotheses for the Brown adjunction are supplied by [sk-lem-brown-hypotheses] for every standing source scheme. We spell out the composition input instead of applying the conditional finite-Tor lemma lem-sf-mate. For composable standing morphisms $T\xrightarrow aS\xrightarrow bR$, the natural lower-shriek comparison $Rb_!Ra_!\cong R(ba)_!$ on $\mathcal T_T$ is [lem-sfb-nonrational-localizing-lower-shriek-composition] when $\Lambda=A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E$, and [lem-sfb-localizing-lower-shriek-composition] when $\Lambda=E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$; $\mathbf Q_\ell$ is its case $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. By [det-sf-existence-brown], all three right adjunctions exist on these same categories. For $M\in\mathcal T_T$ and $N\in\mathcal T_R$, compose their Hom bijections and the lower-shriek comparison to get
$$\Hom(M,a^!b^!N)\cong\Hom(Ra_!M,b^!N)\cong\Hom(Rb_!Ra_!M,N)\cong\Hom(R(ba)_!M,N)\cong\Hom(M,(ba)^!N).$$
This is natural in $M,N$. By [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] it gives a unique isomorphism $a^!b^!\cong(ba)^!$: the inverse natural Hom transformation gives the inverse map, since their composites are identity transformations of representables. Naturality in $N$ follows from faithfulness of the same Yoneda functor. The two successive adjunction bijections are the composite adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], so this is the comparison compatible with the pasted units and counits. No ambient exceptional adjunction or six-functor-datum hypothesis is introduced.

proof.text:
In the Cartesian open-restriction square, $u$ is the inclusion of $f^{-1}(V)$, and $fu=vf_V$ as morphisms. Here are the geometric hypothesis checks. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] the standing schemes are Noetherian, since a field is Noetherian; by [def-weil-constructible-subset] every open and every intersection with an affine open is quasi-compact. The base-change assertion [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] applies directly to $f_V$. An open immersion is separated because its diagonal is an isomorphism, hence a closed immersion, using the diagonal definition of [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Its finite-type property, and the finite-type property of a restriction $fj$, can also be checked from [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]: over an affine in the target choose finitely many affine finite-type charts $\operatorname{Spec}B$ for $f$, and cover the intersection of each chart with $U$ by finitely many principal opens $D(s)$. Their coordinate algebras $B_s$ are finitely generated over the target algebra, by adjoining the generators of $B$ and $s^{-1}$ with relation $ss^{-1}=1$. This proves finite type without an unstated composition theorem. The diagonal of $fj$ is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $f$ to $U\times_YU$, so is closed. The same argument applied to the structure map of $X$ proves that all its opens remain separated finite-type $k$-schemes; apply it to $Y$ as well. Thus every scheme and morphism used here satisfies the standing domain and compactification hypotheses. Thus steps 3 and 4 apply to $(u,f)$ and $(f_V,v)$. Their natural isomorphisms give
$$u^*f^!\cong u^!f^!\cong(fu)^!=(vf_V)^!\cong f_V^!v^!\cong f_V^!v^*.$$
The equality in the middle is transport along the actual equality $fu=vf_V$, using the same compactification functor and its canonical adjoint. For the source restriction, apply step 3 to $j$ and step 4 to the composable pair $(j,f)$; this gives $j^*f^!\cong j^!f^!\cong(fj)^!$. This proves both comparisons in clause (2), with the domains and codomains displayed in the statement.

source.place: Proof (2), the equality fu=v f_V and the two chains; standing geometric hypotheses made explicit.

proof.text: Replace a covering index family by its set of distinct opens in the fixed universe, so it is small. Let $\phi:K\to L$ lie in $\mathcal T_X$ and choose a distinguished triangle $K\xrightarrow\phi L\to C\to K[1]$ in the ambient derived category. The termwise restriction $j_a^*$ is exact on the derived category by [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback], so it gives distinguished triangles after restriction. If all $j_a^*\phi$ are isomorphisms, [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] implies $j_a^*C=0$. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] module restriction is exact and its underlying sheaf functor is naturally identified with inverse image, with the module action transported along the coefficient isomorphism, and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $j_a^*\mathcal H^n(C)\cong\mathcal H^n(j_a^*C)=0$ for every integer $n$. The forgetful functor from ring-object modules to abelian sheaves creates kernels and cokernels: the kernel has the restricted action and the quotient has the induced action, and their universal properties are unchanged. Thus it is exact. The underlying abelian sheaves of these cohomology modules therefore vanish after restriction to every $U_a$. The underlying abelian-sheaf functor of $j_a^*$ is the pullback of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star] with $\mathcal A=\Ab$, and by [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-adjunction] this pullback along the open immersion $j_a$ is computed by restriction: $(j_a^*G)(T\to U_a)\cong G(T\to U_a\to X)$ for every abelian sheaf $G$ on $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$. The localization identification [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] (1) identifies $(U_a)_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ with the slice site $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}/U_a$, so these restrictions are exactly the slice restrictions $r_a$ of the underlying abelian sheaves. They satisfy the covering-sieve hypothesis: for every site object $T\to X$ the open subschemes $T_a=T\times_XU_a$ cover $T$ and map to $U_a$. Every affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset T$ has a finite cover by principal opens $D(s_i)\subset W$, each contained in some $T_{a_i}$, because principal opens form an affine basis and $W$ is quasi-compact. These are affine opens of $T_{a_i}$ and their images cover exactly $W$. Each $T_a\to T$ is flat: its map on the local rings at any point is an isomorphism. Hence $\{T_a\to T\}$ is an fpqc covering by the affine criterion of [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], including the empty affine with the empty subfamily. The $T_a$ are site objects by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] (1) for the open $T_a\to T$. The sieve of arrows with domain admitting a map to some $U_a$ therefore contains a covering family, so is covering by [def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site]. Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism] to the map $0\to\mathcal H^n(C)$ of underlying abelian sheaves. Its slice restrictions are isomorphisms, so $\mathcal H^n(C)=0$. A representative complex of $C$ is consequently acyclic; $0\to C^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism and is inverted in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], whence $C=0$. A final application of [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] makes $\phi$ an isomorphism. Since $\mathcal T_X$ is full, the ambient inverse is also its inverse in $\mathcal T_X$. This argument has no boundedness assumption on $C$.

source.place: Proof (3), cone and cohomology argument; covering-site isomorphism criterion: Stacks Tag 04TQ, sites.tex lemma-glue-maps; exact cohomology: Tag 010N; localization at quasi-isomorphisms: Tag 05RU.

proof.text: Apply clause (2), proved in step 5, to each $j_a:U_a\hookrightarrow X$ and to each $v_b:V_b\hookrightarrow Y$. This gives $j_a^*f^!\cong(fj_a)^!$ and $u_b^*f^!\cong f_{V_b}^!v_b^*$ for the whole localizing categories. Step 6 detects isomorphisms after these restrictions. These are exactly the locality and isomorphism-detection assertions of clause (3). For an empty scheme the same argument says all cohomology sheaves are zero; for the identity cover the comparisons reduce to the same adjunction bijections.

source.place: Proof (3), final two sentences, read as the explicit comparisons in the statement.
